text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers refactor to make programs easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, they might rename unclear variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. The behavior of the software stays exactly the same, so users do not notice any difference. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design decisions are made over time. Although refactoring takes extra effort, it saves time later, because clean code is much easier to update and fix when new problems appear.
